mbm-0043.clue: Why is one ski bright green?
mbm-0043.quote: I painted one ski tip green so my grandfather could pick me out from shore. The first time he waved I waved back with both hands. Now we have a very firm one-hand rule.

mbm-0044.clue: You can find my trail by the little blue threads.
mbm-0044.quote: My scarf caught on a thorn below the summit. Six weeks later I saw the same bright blue wool woven into a wren’s nest. She picked a nice spot.

mbm-0045.clue: We play on the quietest table in town.
mbm-0045.quote: My uncle covered the domino table in felt so my baby cousin could sleep. Now every big winning slam lands with a tiny little puff. We all whisper our arguments too.

mbm-0046.quote: A mint leaf got pressed into my borrowed mystery novel. I read the last chapters in our herb garden so the ending would smell right too.

mbm-0047.clue: The pin flag is sticking out of a bread tin.
mbm-0047.quote: My grandfather taught me to chip on his back lawn. His old bread tin still has a dent from the first shot I made. We turn that side toward the tee for luck.

mbm-0048.clue: Save a little room by the door.
mbm-0048.quote: I nearly missed the last dance carrying in extra chairs. A woman at the end of the line hooked her elbow through mine and the whole circle carried my chair around once.

mbm-0049.clue: I’ve got a box of keys to nothing in particular.
mbm-0049.quote: At the flea market I tried all my odd keys on an old wooden music box. The smallest one worked. I bought it halfway through the first tune.

mbm-0050.clue: My big entrance is six inches tall.
mbm-0050.quote: I built our theater a mouse on wheels for a kitchen scene. I pull it past the stove on fishing line. Even the lead turned to watch it on opening night.

mbm-0051.clue: It’s the only windsock with a darning patch.
mbm-0051.quote: The little airfield let me mend their orange windsock. Now when a plane comes in I can see my crooked blue stitches swing to greet it.

mbm-0052.quote: The day I painted my street it rained before I got to the sky. I tipped the paper and let a drop make the puddle under the bicycle. It knew where to go.

mbm-0053.clue: I keep a typewriter ribbon wrapped round a spoon.
mbm-0053.quote: I ran out of ribbon halfway through a pirate story. My little sister lent me her purple stamp pad. The captain’s last letter came out looking like a ransom note from a plum.

mbm-0054.clue: Can you find which finger has the lights on?
mbm-0054.quote: I painted ten tiny upstairs windows on my nails. One has a yellow lamp and a cat sitting in it. My nephew guesses a different finger before bedtime.

mbm-0055.clue: The rook has a very good dentist.
mbm-0055.quote: Our park rook chipped a corner. A friend who carves soap made us a replacement from a bar of lavender. You can smell my castle coming from three squares away.

mbm-0056.clue: My opponent brought a teapot for the clock.
mbm-0056.quote: The park chess clock broke, so we took turns while an egg timer drained in a teacup. I lost my queen watching the last pink grains fall.

mbm-0057.clue: I’ve spent more time on the sleeve than the card.
mbm-0057.quote: My deck has one magnificent dragon and a dozen chickens. I stitched a tiny feather on the dragon’s sleeve so it remembers who did the work.

mbm-0058.clue: I sing to the stairwell on Tuesdays.
mbm-0058.quote: Our building has a landing where the echo gives me a bass part. Last week it held the note longer than I did. The man downstairs finally stepped out and bowed.

mbm-0059.clue: I leave the page corners alone. The envelopes do the work.
mbm-0059.quote: I found a letter addressed to no one in a library book. It asked what I thought of the ending. I slipped my reply into the same blue envelope and put it back.

mbm-0060.clue: This is the fountain you can hear from the bakery.
mbm-0060.quote: Everybody took pictures of the tower. I followed a tinkling sound into a courtyard and found a toy sailboat going round a fountain. The baker had built the boat from a cake box.

mbm-0061.clue: The oldest card in my deck has a bite mark.
mbm-0061.quote: My rabbit nibbled the corner off my mushroom wizard. The shop gave me a clear sleeve so I could still play it. I let him inspect every victory carrot.

mbm-0062.clue: I brought a lantern for the tournament.
mbm-0062.quote: The card shop lost power with one round left. We played by my camping lantern. Every creature on the table cast a shadow bigger than its owner.

mbm-0063.clue: My best handle started as a mistake.
mbm-0063.quote: The handle slumped while my little pitcher was drying. I cut it loose and turned it sideways. Now it’s a vase with a perch, and my paper bird fits perfectly.

mbm-0064.clue: I save my shiny ones for rainy afternoons.
mbm-0064.quote: When it rains I spread my foil cards near the window and tilt them one at a time. My little cousin calls it the indoor weather forecast. Today she predicted silver hail.

mbm-0065.clue: The bird guide fits behind the curtains.
mbm-0065.quote: I thought the tapping on my kitchen glass was a branch. It was a titmouse getting seeds out of a sunflower head I’d left on the sill. Now I pull up a chair.

mbm-0066.clue: My mother scores the tops with a fork.
mbm-0066.quote: We made so many arepas for my uncle’s birthday that I pressed a birthday candle into the last one. He blew it out before we even got the cheese inside.

mbm-0067.clue: My smallest brush has exactly three hairs.
mbm-0067.quote: I spent all morning painting the reflection in a shop window. Then the shopkeeper came outside and opened it. I turned the page and painted the inside too.
